nodes.name: Voice Intake Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {audio_base64, audio_format, session_id?, turn_id?, duration_seconds?}. One reply node serves every path.

assignments.name: MSG_STT_FAILED
assignments.value: Sorry, I'm having trouble understanding audio right now. Please try again in a moment.

assignments.name: MSG_CLARIFY
assignments.value: Sorry, I didn't catch that. Could you say that again?

assignments.name: MSG_UNSUPPORTED_LANGUAGE
assignments.value: Sorry, I don't support that language yet. Please try again in English, Spanish, French, or German.

assignments.name: MSG_AGENT_FAILED
assignments.value: Sorry, I'm having trouble responding right now. Please try again shortly.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Service URLs, auth, languages, confidence limits, messages, timeouts. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Voice Rules
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for what callers hear and what the agent is told: fixed sentences per language, shortcut phrases answered without the agent, pronunciation fixes for speech, fixed context sent to the agent. Data only; checked on every request. Audio checks, confidence/silence/language judgement and saving rules cannot be changed here.

nodes.name: Validate Request
nodes.notes: Auth, CONFIG sanity and request shape. The audio is decoded and its file signature checked against the declared format, so garbage never reaches the speech-to-text service.

nodes.name: Fetch Session
nodes.notes: 200 {history:[{role,text}]} = continue the conversation. 404 = expired or unknown, start fresh. Anything else = the store is having trouble: carry on without history instead of failing the call.

nodes.name: Interpret Session
nodes.notes: existing | expired (unknown or expired id: gets a fresh server-generated id, never reuses the caller's) | unavailable (store down: keep the caller's id, no history, nothing saved).

nodes.name: Generate Session ID
nodes.notes: Session ids come from n8n's Crypto node (a secure random UUID). They are the only thing protecting a conversation's history, so they must not be guessable. (A Code node cannot use `crypto` in current n8n.)

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { session_id: $json.session_id, history: [], session_status: 'new', can_save: true } }];
return [{ json: $input.first().json }];

nodes.name: Session State
nodes.notes: One place that holds the session for this turn: existing, new or unavailable. Every later node reads it by name.

nodes.name: Prepare Audio
nodes.notes: Builds a proper n8n binary item with the platform helper (a hand-made {data: base64} object is not portable across n8n binary storage modes).

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Multipart upload of the audio (field "file") plus "language". Deliberately NOT neverError: a 5xx throws so retryOnFail really retries (2 tries); after that the error arrives as data and becomes the spoken apology.

nodes.name: Assess Transcript
nodes.notes: stt_failed | silent | low_confidence | unsupported_language | proceed. Confidence is judged only when the service reports it (the old code treated "no segments" as the worst possible confidence, so a Whisper without segments could never get an answer through). Language names and codes (English, en-US) are normalised.

nodes.name: Build Canned Response
nodes.notes: The fixed things the caller hears when we should not or cannot call the agent. Wording is in CONFIG. None of these are saved to the conversation history.

nodes.name: Check Shortcuts
nodes.notes: Runs only for a transcript that passed every check (so silence, low confidence and unsupported languages are never shortcut). A match from the Voice Rules shortcuts answers without calling the agent, and is not saved to the conversation.

parameters.jsCode:
const S = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { outcome: 'shortcut', shortcut: S.shortcut_name, transcript: S.transcript, response_text: S.response_text, language: S.language, degraded: false, warnings: [], session_saved: false } }];

nodes.name: Build Agent Request
nodes.notes: Sends only the most recent MAX_HISTORY_TURNS turns, so a long conversation cannot grow the request forever.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { session_id: $json.session_id, history: $json.history, message: $json.message, language: $json.language, turn_id: $json.turn_id, context: $json.context } }}

nodes.name: Call Agent
nodes.notes: A real JSON body (the old node sent the history array as form text, "[object Object]"). No automatic retry: agents can have side effects.

nodes.name: Interpret Agent
nodes.notes: An empty reply is a failure too: speaking nothing (or an empty string to the TTS engine) is not an answer.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { turn_id: $('Validate Request').first().json.turn_id, user_text: $('Interpret Agent').first().json.transcript, assistant_text: $('Interpret Agent').first().json.response_text } }}

nodes.name: Save Turn
nodes.notes: Only a real, successful exchange is written to history. Creates the session if it is new. turn_id (optional, from the client) lets the store ignore a retried upload of the same turn.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { save: 'skipped' } }];

nodes.name: Assess Save
nodes.notes: If the turn could not be saved the caller still gets the answer, with a warning: the next turn will simply lack this exchange.

nodes.name: Prepare Speech
nodes.notes: The spoken text respects the TTS engine's own limit, cut at a sentence (or word) boundary, and nothing extra is read aloud. The full text always goes back in the response.

nodes.name: Synthesize Speech
nodes.notes: Not neverError, so a 5xx throws and retryOnFail retries (2 tries). If it still fails the caller gets the text without audio.

nodes.name: Build Response
nodes.notes: Reads the synthesized audio with the platform helper, which works whatever binary storage mode n8n uses (reading $binary.data.data directly is not portable across modes). Rejects an empty, oversized or non-audio response.

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.notes: The single reply node. Validation errors, canned replies, failures and answers all build {http_status, response_body} and end here.

nodes.name: Expand QA Archive
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. Blank QA_ARCHIVE_API_URL = no archiving (voice transcripts are personal data, so the default is off).

nodes.name: Archive Interaction
nodes.notes: Best effort, after the reply: a slow or dead archive can never delay or break the caller's answer.

nodes.name: Async Requested?
nodes.notes: Only when ASYNC_MODE allows it AND the caller asked (Prefer: respond-async, or ?async=true; ASYNC_MODE=always means every request). No -> the normal synchronous flow, untouched.

nodes.name: Create Job
nodes.notes: POST /jobs {kind, key, lease_seconds} -> 201 new job {id,...} | 200 {existing:true,...} when this key already has a live or finished job. The STORE makes the (unguessable) id.

nodes.name: Job Verdict
nodes.notes: Created -> accepted. Already exists -> 200 with that job (nothing is started twice). Job store down or odd answer -> 503 and NOTHING started.

nodes.name: Respond Accepted
nodes.notes: The coat-check ticket: 202 with the job id and where to ask, sent straight away. The work carries on after this reply.

nodes.name: Mark Running
nodes.notes: PATCH /jobs/{id} {state:"running", lease_seconds}. Best effort: if it fails the job stays queued and the work still runs.

nodes.name: Async Job? (final)
nodes.notes: The work finished. Async: the reply is saved as the job result. Sync: it is sent to the caller as before.

nodes.name: Save Job Result
nodes.notes: Saves the reply as the job result: succeeded when the reply is 2xx, failed otherwise, with the real http_status and body. Big results lose the optional fields first (marked result_trimmed), then become job_result_too_large. Three tries; if all fail, ops is told.

nodes.name: Webhook: Job Status
nodes.notes: GET ?job_id=... (same token header as the main endpoint). Returns the job state and, when finished, the result the caller would have got synchronously.

nodes.name: Is Job Status?
nodes.notes: Both webhooks share the one CONFIG node, then split here.

nodes.name: Plan Job Status
nodes.notes: Order: auth (401), CONFIG (500), async switched off (404), job_id (400). The status call never starts any work.

nodes.name: Get Job
nodes.notes: GET /jobs/{id} -> 200 job | 404.

nodes.name: Job Status Reply
nodes.notes: Always HTTP 200 for a job that exists: the job's own outcome is in result.http_status. A queued/running job past its lease is reported as failed (worker_lost), so nothing stays "running" forever.

nodes.name: Respond Job Status
nodes.notes: The single reply of the status endpoint.

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: $('Validate Request').first().json }];

nodes.name: Restore Request
nodes.notes: After "Mark Running" the item is the job store's answer, so the validated request is put back here. Every later node reads the request by name.

nodes.name: Expand Job Alerts
nodes.notes: Only when a job result could not be saved. Blank ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL = no alerts (the caller can still see the job go lost in the status endpoint).

nodes.name: Send Job Alert
nodes.notes: Slack-style incoming webhook: POST {text}. Best effort.

parameters.content:
## Voice Intake Pipeline
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the services (the README gives the exact request and response each must answer): speech-to-text, an agent, text-to-speech, a session store.
2. Open **CONFIG**: set `SESSION_API_URL`, `STT_API_URL`, `AGENT_API_URL`, `TTS_API_URL` (the last three are full endpoint URLs). Optional: `VOICE_AUTH_TOKEN`, `QA_ARCHIVE_API_URL`.
3. Activate, then `POST /webhook/voice/intake` with `{audio_base64, audio_format}`.

**Each turn:** validate (decode + check the file signature) -> session -> transcribe -> judge the transcript -> agent (or a fixed reply) -> save the turn -> speak -> reply -> archive.

"I couldn't understand you" is a normal outcome, not an error: silence, low confidence and unsupported languages get a spoken clarification and never reach the agent.
